[element-ref]
=== `<ref>` Reference Item

One item in a bibliographic list, typically a citation describing a referenced work.

#### Usage/Remarks
This element usually contains a citation of some sort, such as a cited standard (<<element-std,`<std>`>>) or a cited book or journal article (<<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>> or <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>).

#### Description

The following, in order: <<element-editing-instruction,`<editing-instruction>`>> <<element-editing-instruction,Editing Instruction>>, zero or more <<element-label,`<label>`>> <<element-label,Label of a Figure, Reference, Etc.>>, zero or one One or more of any of: Citation Elements <<element-citation-alternatives,`<citation-alternatives>`>> <<element-citation-alternatives,Citation Alternatives>> <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>> <<element-element-citation,Element Citation>> <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>> <<element-mixed-citation,Mixed Citation>> <<element-std,`<std>`>> <<element-std,Citation to a Standard>> Standards Note and Example Elements <<element-non-normative-example,`<non-normative-example>`>> <<element-non-normative-example,Non-Normative-Example>> <<element-non-normative-note,`<non-normative-note>`>> <<element-non-normative-note,Non-Normative-Note>> <<element-normative-example,`<normative-example>`>> <<element-normative-example,Normative-Example>> <<element-normative-note,`<normative-note>`>> <<element-normative-note,Normative-Note>> <<element-notes-group,`<notes-group>`>> <<element-notes-group,Notes Group>>

((editing-instruction)*, label?, (citation-alternatives | element-citation | mixed-citation | std | non-normative-note | normative-note | non-normative-example | normative-example | notes-group)+)

#### Tagged Samples

#### Within “Normative references” section

[source,xml]
....
...
<body>
 ...
 <sec sec-type="norm-refs" id="s2">
  <label>2</label>
  <title>Normative references</title>
  <p>The following referenced documents are indispensable 
   for the application of ...</p>
  <ref-list>
   <ref>
    <std type="undated" std-id="iso:std:iso:9001"
     ><std-ref>ISO 9001</std-ref>, 
     <title>Quality management systems &mdash; 
      Requirements</title></std>
   </ref>
   <ref>
    <std type="undated" std-id="iso-iec:std:iso-iec:15415"
     ><std-ref>ISO/IEC 15415</std-ref>, 
     <title>Information technology &mdash; Automatic identification 
      and data capture techniques &mdash; Bar code print quality 
      test specification &mdash; Two-dimensional symbols</title></std>
   </ref>
   ...
  </ref-list>
 </sec>
 ...
</body>
...
....
#### Within named Bibliography

[source,xml]
....
...
<back>
 ...
 <ref-list>
  <title>Bibliography</title>
  <ref id="bibr1">
   <label>[1]</label>
   <mixed-citation>ISO Guide 82, <source>Guidelines for 
    addressing sustainability in standards</source></mixed-citation>
  </ref>
  <ref id="bibr2">
   <label>2</label>
   <std type="undated" std-id="iso:std:iso:9241-11"
    ><std-ref>ISO 9241-11</std-ref>, 
    <title>Ergonomic requirements for office work with visual 
     display terminals (VDTs) &mdash; Part 11: Guidance on 
     usability</title></std>
  </ref>
  ...
 </ref-list>
</back>
...
....
#### Bibliographic reference for journal

[source,xml]
....
...
<ref-list>
 <title>Bibliography</title>
 ...
 <ref id="ref_4">
  <label>4</label>
  <mixed-citation publication-type="journal"
   ><person-group
    ><string-name><surname>Hadorn</surname>,  
     <given-names>H.</given-names></string-name>, 
    <string-name><surname>Z&uuml;rchner</surname>,  
     <given-names>K</given-names></string-name></person-group>. 
   <source>Dtsch. Lebensmitt. Rundsch</source>. 
   <year iso-8601-date="1974">1974</year>, 
   <volume>70</volume> p. <fpage>57</fpage></mixed-citation>
 </ref>
 ...
</ref-list>
...
....
